question: Assume today is 2026-08-15. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park in August 2026, as it will be reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics.

target.what: Recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park as reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics (NPS Visitor Use Statistics). A recreation visit is one person entering the park for recreational purposes; the same person entering multiple times on separate occasions c
target.publisher: National Park Service (NPS), Visitor Use Statistics program
target.cadence: Monthly, typically published with a lag of several weeks to a few months after the month ends
target.caveats: The target period is future relative to the 2026-08-15 cutoff; only partial August 2026 data (if any) would be available. The official figure may be revised. The definition counts recreation visits, not unique visitors; a person entering multiple times counts multiple times. The NPS monthly report m

candidates.hypothesis: August recreation visits in recent years (2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) provide a baseline for the seasonal peak. The 2022 flood caused a sharp drop in June 2022 but August 2022 may have recovered. The 2025 value is the most recent August before the target. A simple projection using recent August levels and trend can estimate August 2026.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly recreation visits for Yellowstone National Park for August 2019, August 2021, August 2022, August 2023, August 2024, and August 2025. Also useful: July and September values for the same years to assess seasonal shape and year-over-year changes. Minimum evidence: at least the most recent August (2025) and the prior year (2024) to compute a growth rate.

candidates.perspective: NPS park-level monthly data for other large western parks
candidates.hypothesis: Visitation trends at comparable parks (e.g., Grand Teton, Glacier, Zion, Yosemite) may correlate with Yellowstone's August visitation, especially if regional travel patterns are similar. A ratio of Yellowstone August visits to a composite of these parks in past years can be applied to their 2026 August data if available.
candidates.data_to_find: August recreation visits for Grand Teton, Glacier, Zion, and Yosemite National Parks for 2024 and 2025, and any partial 2026 data (e.g., July 2026). Minimum evidence: at least one comparable park's August 2025 and July 2026 values to gauge regional trend.

candidates.perspective: Entrance station counts and vehicle traffic
candidates.hypothesis: Yellowstone has five entrances; total recreation visits can be approximated by summing vehicle entries and multiplying by average occupancy, plus pedestrian/bicycle entries. If monthly entrance counts or traffic volumes are available for August 2026 (even partial), they can be scaled to a full month.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly or daily vehicle entry counts at Yellowstone entrances for August 2025 and any available August 2026 data. Average vehicle occupancy rate for Yellowstone in summer. Minimum evidence: total vehicle entries for a recent August and an occupancy factor.

candidates.hypothesis: Overnight stays in Yellowstone (lodges, campgrounds) are a component of visitation. Total recreation visits correlate with overnight stays, but day visits dominate. If occupancy rates and room/campsite counts are available for August 2026, they can help estimate overnight visitors, which can be combined with day-use estimates.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone lodging occupancy rates and available rooms/campsites for August 2025 and 2026 (if available). Number of overnight stays reported by Xanterra or NPS. Minimum evidence: total overnight stays in August 2025 and any indication of 2026 bookings.

candidates.hypothesis: Any major closures (e.g., road construction, flood damage, government shutdown) or unusual weather in August 2026 could significantly alter visitation. The 2022 flood caused a temporary drop; similar events in 2026 would need to be accounted for.
candidates.data_to_find: News reports of Yellowstone closures or disruptions in July-August 2026. Road construction schedules for 2026. Weather anomalies (e.g., heat waves, wildfires) affecting travel. Minimum evidence: any confirmed closure or event that would reduce access.

candidates.hypothesis: National or regional tourism forecasts for summer 2026 may indicate whether travel to national parks is up or down. If a forecast for Yellowstone specifically exists, it can be used directly.
candidates.data_to_find: Summer 2026 travel forecasts for national parks or the Mountain West. Any NPS or third-party projections for Yellowstone visitation in 2026. Minimum evidence: a qualitative or quantitative forecast for 2026 park visitation.

candidates.hypothesis: August typically accounts for a stable share of Yellowstone's annual recreation visits (e.g., around 20-25%). If a reliable estimate of total 2026 annual visits is available (or can be projected from year-to-date data), multiplying by the August share yields the target.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone annual recreation visits for 2024 and 2025, and year-to-date 2026 visits through July. Historical August share of annual visits for 2019, 2021-2025. Minimum evidence: August share from at least two recent years and a 2026 year-to-date total.

candidates.hypothesis: Google Trends or social media mentions for Yellowstone may correlate with visitation, but the relationship is noisy. If a strong correlation is established historically, current attention levels could indicate whether August 2026 is above or below trend.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends data for 'Yellowstone National Park' for summer 2025 and 2026. Social media post volumes. Minimum evidence: a time series of search interest aligned with monthly visitation to estimate elasticity.

methods.rationale: Uses the observed July 2026 NPS figure (958,706) and a park-specific July-to-August ratio anchored on the 2014-2018 NPS monthly averages and recent years. Shared dependency: both the July 2026 level and the ratio come from NPS measurement conventions, so a definitional change in NPS counting would affect both. Failure mode: an August-specific shock (closure, smoke, policy) not reflected in July.

assumptions.name: August 2026 recreation visits as a fraction of July 2026 recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: Park-specific July-to-August ratio. From the 2014-2018 NPS monthly averages (p141, p142), August/July = 839,787/947,688 = 0.886. Recent years are consistent: 2025 881,936/975,109 = 0.904; 2024 868,259/975,109-like July 2024 is not directly available, but 2023 846,389/969,692 = 0.873; 2021 921,844/1,080,767 = 0.853. The range spans these observed ratios.
assumptions.applies_when: August 2026 has no major access closure or demand shock relative to July 2026, and the park's seasonal July-to-August pattern remains similar to 2014-2025.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a major August 2026 closure, wildfire smoke event, or policy change that materially shifts August relative to July; or an observed August 2026 value far outside the ratio range.

assumptions.name: August 2026 recreation visits as a fraction of August 2025 recreation visits
assumptions.rationale: Recent 2026 monthly NPS releases show mild softness versus 2025: June 2026 down 3% (p122), July 2026 down 2% (p72), YTD through July 2026 down 1% (p76). A near-flat August 2026 versus August 2025 is the central case, with uncertainty spanning roughly -7% to +3%.
assumptions.applies_when: The mild 2026 softness seen in June and July continues into August, with no new shock.
assumptions.falsified_by: A major August 2026 shock (closure, smoke, policy) or a sharp reversal in the 2026 trend.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
